clue.text: Creditable narratives?

parts.note: stories that could be believed, read again as bookkeeping records with a credit column, statements of money owed and paid

explanation.definitionFit: Accounts are narratives or reports of events, and also financial records where credits are entered.

clue.text: Alarming thing for the soldier poet?

definitions.text: Alarming thing for the soldier poet?

parts.words: Alarming thing for the soldier poet
parts.note: an alarm rung in a military encampment, which split differently is the surname of a Scottish poet

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Alarming thing for the soldier' as a bell in an army camp; the same letters name Thomas Campbell, the Scottish poet of 'Ye Mariners of England'.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Campbell was a Scottish poet famous for martial verse; a camp bell is the alarm that rouses soldiers.

clue.text: Native quarters ?

parts.note: natives are oysters bred in British waters, and their quarters are the homes they live in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Native' looks like a local inhabitant, but a native is an oyster raised in British beds (Whitstable natives), so its quarters are the shells it lives in.
explanation.definitionFit: A native is a cultivated British oyster, whose living quarters are the hard casings it grows.

clue.text: Moriarty was "the —— of crime"

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Sherlock Holmes calls Professor Moriarty the French emperor of crime in 'The Final Problem'

explanation.walkthrough: Holmes describes Moriarty as 'the Napoleon of crime', a master organiser, in Conan Doyle's 'The Final Problem'; the solver fills the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Holmes compares Moriarty to the French emperor because he commands a vast criminal empire.

clue.text: Learning about one fabulous bird, love? Nothing but wind

indicators.note: the abbreviation for learning goes about, round the next pieces

parts.note: learning is science, abbreviated Sc as in the degree BSc
one is I, the Roman numeral
the roc is the giant bird of Arabian fable
love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A scholar's knowledge of mythical birds and romance turns out to be empty bluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing but' leads to the definition: the learning amounts to mere wind. 'about' puts I and ROC inside SC.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot dusty wind blowing from North Africa across the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Riddle set by Egan-I'm involved

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzle composed by a setter called Egan, who admits a part in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' scrambles EGANIM, the letters of 'Egan-I'm'.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzle or mystery, a synonym for a riddle.

clue.text: She may be upset

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, and this name reads the same from the bottom up

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A woman who is easily offended.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is a palindrome, so when 'upset' (read upwards in a down clue) it is unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a woman's name, so it can stand for any she.

clue.text: Course of study on Great War battle

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
the Somme was a battle of the First World War, 1916

explanation.surface: A curriculum on the history of the First World War's battles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course of study' looks like one phrase, but 'Course' is a dinner course.
explanation.definitionFit: Consommé is a clear soup served as one course of a meal.

clue.text: Allusive remark upset union — it's about a tip

indicators.note: the rearranged union goes about, round, the next piece
upset means knocked over or disordered, so the letters of union are rearranged

parts.note: a tip is an end or extremity

explanation.surface: An insinuating comment that annoyed a trade union concerning a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns UNION into INNUO, and 'about' wraps that round END (a tip).
explanation.definitionFit: An innuendo is an indirect hint, usually a suggestive or disparaging one.

clue.text: Prophet in Utopia, most likely ?

indicators.note: in says the answer sits within the letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A seer would most probably be found in an ideal imaginary land.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'UtopiA MOSt'; 'likely' just completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos was one of the minor Hebrew prophets of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Musical part, of a complete fish

parts.note: thorough means complete or absolute
the bass is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Seems to ask what part of an entire fish might be musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorough bass is an old name for the figured bass line in Baroque music.

clue.text: Bad rig-rent to repair skipper arranges that

indicators.note: repair means mend or set right, so these letters are rearranged into new order

explanation.surface: A captain sorts out a broken boat's rig and its tear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skipper' suggests a boat, but here he is a cricket captain, who decides who goes in to bat when. 'repair' rearranges BADRIGRENTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket captain decides the sequence in which his team's players go in to bat.

clue.text: Reward for the scholarly half-back for example?

definitions.meaning: an award a university gives to a student who completes a course
half of the word back is BA, the Bachelor of Arts award, so it is an example

explanation.walkthrough: 'half-back' looks like a football position, but read it as half the word 'back': BA, which is one such academic award.
explanation.definitionFit: A university awards a qualification such as a BA to a successful student.

clue.text: Principles for reform 'of Christmas showed endless change

indicators.note: change means alter, so the remaining letters are rearranged
endless means without its final letter, so the last letter of the word Christmas goes

explanation.surface: Proposals for reforming the festive season show it never stops changing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the final S of Christmas, and 'change' rearranges CHRISTMA. Chartism was a 1830s-40s British working-class movement for votes for all men, set out in the People's Charter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chartism held to the six points of the People's Charter, a programme of parliamentary reform.

clue.text: A number object in Iceland's parliament

parts.note: L is fifty in Roman numerals
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Something numbered among the exhibits in the Icelandic assembly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure on show but the Roman numeral L.
explanation.definitionFit: The Althing is the national assembly of Iceland, one of the oldest parliaments.

clue.text: Taking things for granted ? That's arrogant

explanation.definitionFit: To assume is to suppose without proof, and an assuming manner is presumptuous and haughty.

clue.text: Shorten important part in "Horatius"?

definitions.meaning: in Macaulay's poem Horatius holds a river crossing against the Etruscan army

explanation.walkthrough: Split it as A BRIDGE: in Macaulay's 'Horatius' the hero keeps the bridge over the Tiber against the invading army.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge is to cut a text down; a bridge is the key scene of Macaulay's poem.

clue.text: Native quarter without a singer

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the native's letters go round the next piece

parts.note: a Briton is a native of Britain
a quarter is a compass point, here E for east

explanation.surface: An area inhabited by locals with no one to sing in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking: BRITON goes round A, then E (east, a compass quarter) follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A baritone is a male singer whose voice lies between tenor and bass.

clue.text: Traps fish to get drink

parts.note: gins are snares or traps for game
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A fisherman sets traps to catch fish and earn himself a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traps' is a noun, plural snares, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin sling is a cocktail of gin with sugar, water and lemon.

clue.text: Measures taken by unions

definitions.meaning: old units of distance of about three miles
alliances or associations of clubs or states

explanation.definitionFit: A league is an old distance of about three miles, and also an alliance of members.

clue.text: "The last —— of recorded time" (Macbeth)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Macbeth's 'Tomorrow, and tomorrow' speech

explanation.walkthrough: Macbeth's speech runs 'Creeps in this petty pace from day to day, To the last syllable of recorded time'; the solver supplies the missing word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's line imagines time as speech, ending on its final unit of sound.

clue.text: Wagers about a quarter of the animals

indicators.note: the bets go about, round the next pieces

parts.note: bets are wagers
a quarter is a compass point, here S for south

explanation.surface: Gamblers' stakes on roughly a fourth of the creatures in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'roughly', but it puts A and S (south) inside BETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Beasts is a general word for animals, especially four-footed ones.

clue.text: Very violent, spirit appears in horseplay

indicators.note: in places the spirit inside the word for horseplay

parts.note: a rag is a boisterous student prank or horseplay
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Rough play turns savage when alcohol gets involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like a ghost or temper, but it is the drink GIN, put 'in' RAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Raging means furious and violent, as a raging storm.

clue.text: Chap's reaction to a joke is simply killing !

parts.note: a chap is a man, with the possessive s
laughter is how one reacts to a joke

explanation.surface: A fellow says a joke is simply killing, meaning it is very funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'killing' looks like 'hilarious', which fits the joke picture, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Manslaughter is the crime of unlawful killing without malice aforethought.

clue.text: These hot tips turn up in bridge?

indicators.note: in a down entry turn up means read from bottom to top, so the word for bridge is backwards

parts.note: a span is a bridge, or the stretch of one

explanation.surface: Racing tips that come up during a game of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: A nap is a racing tipster's most confident selection. 'bridge' suggests the card game, but it is SPAN, which 'turn up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A nap is a newspaper tipster's strongest racing tip of the day.

clue.text: Commonly, a bit of a wet

definitions.text: Commonly, a bit of a wet

parts.words: Commonly, a bit of a wet
parts.note: a single falling drop of water, and in common slang a feeble, weak person, someone wet

explanation.walkthrough: A drop of water is literally a little bit of the wet; in slang ('commonly') a wet is a weakling.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop of liquid is a small bit of moisture, and colloquially a feeble person is a weed.

clue.text: No longer sorry I've had this drink

definitions.text: No longer sorry I've had this drink

parts.words: No longer sorry I've had this drink
parts.note: a potion that takes away grief and sorrow, from Greek myth and Homer's Odyssey

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like someone who has stopped regretting a drink, but the drink itself, in Greek legend, banishes sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepenthe is the drug of forgetfulness in Homer that frees the drinker from grief.

clue.text: Main class of guide — mature

parts.note: to steer is to guide
to age is to mature or ripen

explanation.surface: The principal category of guidance is maturity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, as in 'the Spanish Main', so 'Main class' is a class of travel at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Steerage is the cheapest class of passage on an ocean liner.
